defects.canonical: The amount is rounded to whole minor units BEFORE the exchange-rate conversion (value*100 is quantized, then multiplied by rate), contrary to the documented contract that requires converting first and rounding to minor units last. Rounding the pre-conversion value discards sub-unit precision, producing systematic drift after the rate is applied.
defects.why_subtle: Both a *100 scaling and a quantize appear, so the code looks like correct minor-unit handling; the reviewer has to notice the rate is applied after the rounding, not before.

defects.canonical: get_rate(currency) is invoked once per amount inside the loop even when many amounts share the same currency, repeating an avoidable (and potentially expensive) rate lookup; the result should be memoized/cached per currency across iterations.
defects.why_subtle: Calling get_rate per amount reads as ordinary correct code; the redundancy is only visible when you realize amounts commonly share currencies and the lookup is non-trivial.
